title: Author Augusto Cury Debuts in Debates and Runs for President
seoTitle: Author Augusto Cury Runs for President, Joins Debates
subtitle: Known for his self-help books, the psychiatrist is running for president under the Avante party in the 2026 elections.
excerpt: Learn about Augusto Cury, the author and psychiatrist running for Brazil's presidency in the 2026 elections under the Avante party.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Augusto Cury's name is trending following his debut in televised debates for the 2026 presidential race. Nationally known as a psychiatrist, lecturer, and self-help author, he is running for the Planalto Palace under the Avante party.

Who is Augusto Cury and His Background

At 67 years old, the author has swapped his books for the campaign trail to run for the federal executive's highest office. Before entering his first televised debate, Cury caught the press's attention by threatening to drop out of the event in protest against the absences of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, though he eventually reversed course and participated in the face-off.

The Campaign and the Electoral Race

Running for Avante, Cury states that his main obstacle in the electoral race is a lack of name recognition among a large portion of the electorate. In voter polling released before the debate, the psychiatrist polled between 1% and 2%. His campaign team is focused on attracting undecided voters, those who cast blank or spoiled ballots, and those who abstain from voting.

Proposals and Political Vision

During his public appearances and interviews, Cury defines his political stance with the motto of having "a capitalist mind and a social heart." He advocates for a lean, efficient state combined with human rights and social protection agendas. Among his proposals for Brazil are structural changes to the branches of government, including modifications to the presidential system through the creation of a prime minister post and reforms to the Supreme Federal Court, such as ending lifetime appointments for its justices.

Criticism of Polarization and the Political Climate

During the televised confrontation, the author criticized political polarization and the level of aggressiveness among the candidates. He presented himself as an alternative to the groups that, in his view, dominate the national race, claiming to be the only candidate capable of leading a pact to rebuild the country and unite different political factions.

With information from O GLOBO, BBC.
